AA.II.A.K2.text: Determining that the aircraft to be used is appropriate, airworthy, and in a condition for safe flight by locating and explaining related documents such as:

AA.II.A.K2b.text: b. Operating limitations, handbooks, and manuals

AA.II.A.K2c.text: c. Minimum Equipment List (MEL) and Configuration Deviation List (CDL), Kinds of Operations Equipment Lists (KOEL)

AA.II.A.K2e.text: e. Required inspections or tests and appropriate records and documentation (e.g., dispatch release) as applicable to the proposed flight or operation

AA.II.A.K3.text: Preventive maintenance that can be performed by the pilot or other designated crewmember.

AA.II.A.K4a.text: a. Which items should be inspected

AA.II.A.K4b.text: b. The reasons for checking each item

AA.II.A.K4c.text: c. How to detect possible defects

AA.II.A.K5.text: Environmental factors, including weather, terrain, route selection, and obstructions.

AA.II.A.K6.text: Requirements for current and appropriate navigation data.

AA.II.A.K7.text: Operations specifications, management specifications, or letters of authorization applying to a particular aircraft and operation, if applicable.

AA.II.A.R2.text: Inoperative equipment discovered prior to flight.

AA.II.A.R3.text: Environment (e.g., weather, airports, airspace, terrain, obstacles).

AA.II.A.S1.text: Inspect the aircraft in accordance with an appropriate checklist demonstrating proper operation of applicable airplane systems. Coordinate checklist with crew, if appropriate.

AA.II.A.S2.text: Coordinate with ground crew and ensure adequate clearance prior to moving doors, hatches, flight control surfaces, etc.

AA.II.A.S3.text: Document any discrepancies found; take corrective action and acknowledge limitations imposed by MEL/CDL items, if applicable.

AA.II.A.S4.text: Determine if the aircraft is airworthy and in condition for safe flight.

AA.II.A.S5.text: Identify and comply with operations specifications as required.

AA.II.A.S6.text: Assess factors related to the environment (weather, airports, terrain, airspace).

AA.II.A.S7.text: Ensure the airplane and surfaces are free of ice, snow, and frost. If icing conditions are present, demonstrate satisfactory knowledge of deicing procedures.

AA.II.B.K1.text: Normal and abnormal powerplant start procedures and limitations, including the use of an auxiliary power unit (APU) or external power source, if applicable.

AA.II.B.K3.text: Malfunctions during powerplant start, procedures to address the malfunction, and any associated limitations.

AA.II.B.K4.text: Coordinating and communicating with ground personnel for powerplant start, if applicable.

AA.II.B.R3.text: Managing situations where specific instructions or checklist items are not published.

AA.II.B.R4.text: Personnel, vehicles, vessels, foreign object debris, and other aircraft in the vicinity during powerplant start.

AA.II.B.S1.text: Ensure the ground safety procedures are followed during the before-start, start, and after-start phases.

AA.II.B.S2.text: Use appropriate ground crew personnel during the start procedures (if applicable). 14

AA.II.B.S3.text: Coordinate with crew, if applicable, and complete the appropriate checklist(s) prior to and after powerplant start.

AA.II.B.S4.text: Respond appropriately to an abnormal start or malfunction.

AA.II.C.K1.text: Current airport aeronautical references and information resources such as the Chart Supplement, airport diagram, and Notices to Air Missions (NOTAMs).

AA.II.C.K10.text: Low visibility taxi operations and techniques used to avoid disorientation.

AA.II.C.K2.text: Taxi instructions/clearances, including published taxi routes.

AA.II.C.K4.text: Appropriate aircraft lighting for day and night operations.

AA.II.C.K6.text: Appropriate flight deck activities prior to taxi, including route planning, identifying the location of Hot Spots, and coordinating with crew if, applicable.

AA.II.C.K7.text: Communications at towered and nontowered airports.

AA.II.C.R1.text: Distractions, task prioritization, loss of situational awareness, or disorientation.

AA.II.C.R2.text: Confirmation or expectation bias as related to taxi instructions.

AA.II.C.R3.text: A taxi route or departure runway change.

AA.II.C.S1.text: Receive/record taxi instructions, read back/acknowledge taxi clearances, and review taxi routes on the airport diagram.

AA.II.C.S2.text: Use an appropriate airport diagram or taxi chart, if published. 15

AA.II.C.S3.text: Comply with air traffic control (ATC) clearances and instructions and observe all runway hold lines, Instrument Landing System (ILS) critical areas, beacons, and other airport/taxiway markings and lighting.

AA.II.C.S4.text: Coordinate with crew, if applicable, and complete the appropriate checklist(s) prior to and during taxi, as appropriate.

AA.II.C.S6.text: Maintain correct and positive airplane control, proper speed, appropriate use of wheel brakes and reverse thrust, and separation between other aircraft, vehicles, and persons to avoid an incursion/ incident/accident.

AA.II.C.S7.text: Demonstrate taxi during day and night operations. If either condition is not available, the applicant explains the differences between day and night taxi.

AA.II.C.S8.text: Demonstrate proper use of aircraft exterior lighting for day and night operations. If either condition is not available, the applicant explains the differences between exterior aircraft lighting used for day and night operations.

AA.II.C.S9.text: Explain the hazards of low visibility taxi operations.

AA.II.D.K1.text: Current airport/seaplane base aeronautical references and information resources, including Chart Supplements, airport diagram, and appropriate references.

AA.II.D.K3.text: Airport/seaplane base markings, signs, and lights.

AA.II.D.K4.text: Appropriate aircraft lighting for day and night operations.

AA.II.D.K5.text: Sailing elements and techniques and when sailing should be used.

AA.II.D.K6.text: Considerations for determining the most favorable sailing course.

AA.II.D.K7a.text: a. Appropriate flight deck activities prior to taxi or sailing, including route planning, and coordinating with crew, if applicable

AA.II.D.K7b.text: b. Communications at towered and nontowered seaplane bases

AA.II.D.K7c.text: c. Entering or crossing runways (land operation)

AA.II.D.K7d.text: d. Night taxi and sailing operations

AA.II.D.K7e.text: e. Low visibility taxi and sailing operations

AA.II.D.R1.text: Distractions, task prioritization, loss of situational awareness, or disorientation. 16

AA.II.D.R4.text: Low visibility taxi and sailing operations.

AA.II.D.R6.text: Gear position in an amphibious airplane.

AA.II.D.R7.text: Confirmation or expectation bias as related to taxi instructions.

AA.II.D.S1.text: Receive/record taxi instructions, read back/acknowledge taxi clearances, and review taxi routes on the airport diagram.

AA.II.D.S10.text: Exhibit procedures for steering and maneuvering while maintaining proper situational awareness and desired orientation, path, and position.

AA.II.D.S11.text: Plan and follow the most favorable taxi or sailing course for current conditions.

AA.II.D.S12.text: Demonstrate taxi or sailing during day and night operations. If either condition is not available, the applicant explains the differences between day and night taxi or sailing.

AA.II.D.S13.text: Demonstrate proper use of aircraft exterior lighting for day and night operations. If either condition is not available, the applicant explains the differences between exterior aircraft lighting used for day and night operations.

AA.II.D.S14.text: Explain the hazards of low visibility taxi and sailing operations.

AA.II.D.S2.text: Use an appropriate chart during taxi, if published.

AA.II.D.S3.text: Comply with ATC clearances, as appropriate, and seaplane base/airport/taxiway markings, signals and signs.

AA.II.D.S4.text: Depart the dock/mooring buoy or beach/ramp in a safe manner, considering wind, current, traffic, and hazards.

AA.II.D.S5.text: Coordinate with crew, if applicable, and complete the appropriate checklist(s) prior to and during taxi or sailing, as appropriate.

AA.II.D.S7.text: Maintain correct and positive airplane control, proper speed, appropriate use of reverse thrust, and separation between other aircraft, vehicles, vessels, and persons to avoid an incursion or right-of-way violation.

AA.II.D.S8.text: Position the flight controls, flaps, doors, water rudders, and power correctly for the existing conditions to follow the desired course while sailing and to prevent or correct for porpoising and skipping during step taxi.

AA.II.D.S9.text: Use the appropriate idle, plow, or step taxi technique.

AA.II.E.K1.text: Purpose of pre-takeoff checklist items, including:

AA.II.E.K1a.text: a. Reasons for checking each item

AA.II.E.K1c.text: c. Ensuring the aircraft is in safe operating condition

AA.II.E.K2.text: Deicing and anti-icing procedures, holdover times, and pre-takeoff contamination check.

AA.II.E.K3.text: Adverse weather considerations for performance on takeoff (e.g., snow, ice, gusting crosswinds, low- visibility).

AA.II.E.K4.text: Items to be included in a before takeoff briefing.

AA.II.E.R1.text: Division of attention while conducting before takeoff checks.

AA.II.E.R2.text: An unexpected change in the runway to be used for departure.

AA.II.E.R3.text: Using performance data to set airspeeds and flight instruments for actual conditions and the departure runway.

AA.II.E.R4.text: Setting navigation and communication equipment for departure.

AA.II.E.R5.text: Configuring autopilot and flight director for departure.

AA.II.E.R6.text: Adverse weather conditions prior to takeoff (e.g., snow, ice, gusting crosswinds, low-visibility).

AA.II.E.R7.text: Potential powerplant failure during takeoff or other malfunction considering operational factors such as airplane characteristics, runway/takeoff path length, surface conditions, environmental conditions, and obstructions.

AA.II.E.S1.text: Determine the airplane’s takeoff performance for actual conditions and planned departure runway or waterway.

AA.II.E.S2.text: Coordinate with crew, if applicable, and complete the appropriate checklist(s) prior to takeoff in a timely manner.

AA.II.E.S3.text: Determine all systems checked are within an acceptable operating range and are safe for the proposed flight. During the checks, explain at the request of the evaluator, any system operating characteristic or limitation and any corrective action for a malfunction.

AA.II.E.S4.text: Determine airspeeds/V-speeds and set flight instruments appropriately, configure flight director, autopilot, and navigation and communication equipment for the current flight conditions and takeoff and departure clearances.

AA.II.E.S5.text: Conduct a briefing that includes procedures for emergency and abnormal situations (e.g., powerplant failure, windshear), which may be encountered during takeoff, and state the planned action if they were to occur.

AA.II.E.S6.text: Obtain and correctly interpret the takeoff and departure clearance. 18
